title: Reconstructing a graph from its Bell colouring graph
summary: The Bell colouring graph $\mathcal{B}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the partitions of the vertex set of $G$ into independent sets, with an edge between two partitions if and only if one can be obtained from the other by changing the part of a single vertex of $G$. Given a natural number $k$, the Bell $k$-colouring graph $\mathcal{B}_k(G)$ and the upper-Bell $k$-colouring graph $\mathcal{B}_{\geq k}(G)$ are the induced subgraphs of $\mathcal{B}(G)$ consisting of all partitions with at most $k$ parts and at least $k$ parts, respectively.
